subject: Private deploy: edge attachment validation and port-binding evidence
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novamed.com>, Dave Park <dave.park@novamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deploy: edge attachment validation and port-binding evidence

Hi Elena / Dave,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we prepare the cutover window on the 29th, can you please validate the following items so we can clear the last operational checks on our side: 

- Confirm the edge attachment (L3 demarc) is advertised on your fabric and the subnets in the attached diagram (redwood-boundary-diagram-v2.pdf) are present.
- Export of the firewall ACLs for the attachment (CSV) showing the rules allowing the control-plane TLS (TCP 443) and runtime token egress to the Redwood endpoints.
- A short port-binding evidence log from your NAT/edge device showing the test session we ran at 15:05 PDT yesterday (port-binding-evidence.log).

If you can drop the ACL CSV and the port-binding log into the shared drive link below, that will be perfect. The acceptance criteria we need are:
  * Control-plane TLS handshake observed from NovaMed IP 3.45.234.11 -> redwood-control-1:443
  * Runtime egress permitted for 52.14.XX.XX/32 with established flows to our runtime pool (we will share the precise IPs in the ticket)

We only need the artifacts — screenshots are fine if the device doesn't export CSVs easily.

Thanks,
Mateo
Site Reliability Eng, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novamed.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Dave Park <dave.park@novamed.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: edge attachment validation and port-binding evidence

Hi Mateo — thanks, checking a few things now. Attached is the firewall ACL export (novamed-firewall-acl-export-20270424.csv) and a short capture showing the control-plane TLS from your IP. 

We see the session from 3.45.234.11 -> 54.23.11.9:443 established at 2027-04-24T15:05:11Z. Runtime egress to 52.14.10.23 shows ALLOW with state ESTABLISHED in the same export.

A couple of notes:
- Our edge device does NAT to 198.51.100.12 for outbound; we've included a small port-binding text log (port-binding-evidence.log).
- We left an inline comment in the CSV for the rule ID 213: we currently have a source port range pinned to 32768-60999 per appliance default. If you need a single source port, we'll have to add a static port map for the test.

Forwarding the drive link where I dropped the two files.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Network Operations Manager, NovaMed

Date: 2027-04-26T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: edge attachment validation and port-binding evidence

Thanks Elena — that's great evidence. Quick checklist from our side (what we will verify during the cutover):

1) Control-plane TLS: we need the client IP -> redwood-control-1:443 handshake present (you included that, good).
2) Runtime egress: we will validate flows from your NAT IPs to our runtime pool and verify token exchange in the trace.
3) Port-binding: the default ephemeral range is OK for general traffic, but for our warm-up tooling we prefer consistent source ports during the brief test window. Please add the static port map for the staging VLAN (if you can) or confirm we can rely on the NAT IP + ephemeral range.

Acceptance: if the two artifacts (CSV + log) match the items above we'll mark the boundary as "validated" and proceed with the scheduled cutover on 2027-04-29 22:00-23:30 PDT. If you want, we can do a 15-minute pre-cutover smoke at 21:30.

Marissa
Sr. Customer Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novamed.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: edge attachment validation and port-binding evidence

Small technical addendum from our infra review:

- If NovaMed's edge NATs all outbound to 198.51.100.12, our runtime pool will see sessions from that address; that's OK. However, the control-plane pinning we use for some warm-up flows expects consistent source ephemeral ports across the flow (the warm-up sequencer does port rotation testing).
- Workaround A (recommended for the short window): add a 1:1 static port map for the single test host in the staging VLAN.
- Workaround B: we can instrument our client to accept ephemeral source ranges — this requires a minor test harness change on our side and will add ~10 minutes prep.

If you prefer we can do option B to avoid touching your NAT config; either way we need confirmation before 27th EOD.

Jonas
Principal Infra Eng, Redwood Inference

> > Hi Mateo — thanks, checking a few things now. Attached is the firewall ACL export...
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novamed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-27T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: edge attachment validation and port-binding evidence

Elena / team — thanks for the quick turn. Confirming acceptance criteria:

- We reviewed novamed-firewall-acl-export-20270424.csv and the inline comment for rule 213; that rule permits the control-plane TLS flows we listed.
- The port-binding-evidence.log shows the NAT translation to 198.51.100.12 and the sequential ephemeral source ports used during the test. Jonas — we can proceed with Workaround B for the staging warm-up (Redwood will adapt the sequencer for ephemeral ranges) to minimize changes on your side.

Action items:
- NovaMed: leave the CSV & log in the Drive folder linked in the ticket (done).
- Redwood (Marissa/Jonas): update the warm-up sequencer to accept ephemeral ranges and provide a one-paragraph test run playbook by 2027-04-28 12:00 PDT.
- All: 15-minute pre-cutover smoke at 2027-04-29 21:30 PDT.

If anything else crops up I will escalate, otherwise we will mark the boundary validated and proceed.

Thanks everyone — appreciate the fast turnaround.

Mateo
Site Reliability Eng, Redwood Inference
